definitions.meaning: an honourable person is honest and principled
a post is a vertical pole or support standing straight up

explanation.definitionFit: An honest, principled person is called this, and a vertical pole set straight in the ground is also one.

definitions.meaning: a thick cosmetic foundation used in theatre
Shrove Tuesday is traditionally celebrated by eating flat batter cakes

explanation.surface: A question about what cosmetics to wear on a particular weekday.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday, before Lent, is known in Britain as Pancake Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancake make-up is a stage foundation, and the batter food is eaten on Shrove Tuesday.

clue.text: Useless writer turns up in it

indicators.note: the reversed writer sits inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A useless author appears in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turns up' means read upwards, so the writer word runs backwards before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and incompetent, lacking skill: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Crafty sleuth catches king with cheat

indicators.note: a crafty rearrangement of the letters of sleuth

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A clever detective arrests a monarch alongside a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' makes HUSTLE from sleuth; R for king follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or con artist, someone who cheats people out of money.

definitions.meaning: to cause wild uproar and disorder
to behave without any control, like weeds spreading everywhere

explanation.surface: A description of someone causing trouble and behaving without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to create an uproar and to behave or spread without any checks.

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces are sent by the United Nations
disinterested means impartial or fair, which is just

explanation.surface: Neutral peacekeepers turn out to be villains.
explanation.walkthrough: Disinterested means impartial, not uninterested, so it gives JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair and morally wrong; wicked here means acting without justice.

indicators.note: the letters of dreamer and in are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleeper whose rest is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like part of the disturbed-sleep picture, but it is the definition, meaning what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest means what is left over, the remaining part.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
verse is poetry, a poem
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A romantic poem by a foreign writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas, foreign: coming from a land across the sea.

definitions.meaning: cash given as a gift, intended as a present
for now, for the time being

explanation.surface: A gift of cash for a birthday, for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Money meant as a gift, and an idiom meaning for the time being.

indicators.note: the letters are shown within the word concerts, as if appearing in it

explanation.surface: Something that used to be part of a musical programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at one time in the past: a direct adverb synonym.

parts.note: to bare is to expose or show
a jumper is a knitted top, a sweater

explanation.surface: A rider in a contest wearing nothing on the upper body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With bare top' suggests a topless rider, but bare is a verb meaning show and top is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor on horseback who rides a course of fences in an equestrian event.

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Dad's phone comes in a pale shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft, pale shades of colour are described by this word, like chalk drawing tones.

clue.text: Most flavoursome wine in the analysis

indicators.note: the wine is placed inside the word for analysis

parts.note: a test is an analysis or examination
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A wine-tasting report naming the best-flavoured bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of tasty, meaning having the strongest, most pleasant flavour.

parts.note: blood-stained things are red
a runner is a long narrow carpet

explanation.surface: An injured athlete in need of special attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is a strip of carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish ceremonial welcome given to celebrities, named after the strip rolled out for them.

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to come in or arrive

explanation.surface: Fried potatoes waiting for the fish to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' suggests fish and chips; it is the traditional nickname for a ship's woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is a traditional nickname for a woodworker, who makes wood chips.

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed after the word for theory

parts.note: an idea is a theory or notion

explanation.surface: A flawless theory has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' reads as abandoned, but left gives L and behind places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: flawless, exactly as one would wish.

definitions.meaning: a mark or scratch cut into a surface, or a tally of points
the current state of affairs, as in knowing what's what

explanation.surface: A note about recording how matters currently stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch or tally mark is one sense; the idiomatic 'know the state of play' gives the other.

definitions.meaning: kicks taken from the flag at the angle of the pitch

explanation.surface: Asking where footballers go to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks used as retreats, and football set pieces taken from the pitch's angles.

clue.text: Man in the moon has a limb well-made

parts.note: an arm is a limb
something well-made is strong and sturdy

explanation.surface: The face in the moon has a sturdy arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man in the moon' is the folklore face, but here it is Neil Armstrong, first person to walk on the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong was literally a man on the moon in 1969, the first astronaut to step onto it.

explanation.surface: Asking which English poet paid up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet, and someone who pays out money is one too.

clue.text: Support could be distributed in hours

indicators.note: the letters of in hours could be spread out into a different order

explanation.surface: Help might be handed out over a number of hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed or sustain someone, providing what they need to grow.

clue.text: Coma is unsettled by this pattern

indicators.note: the letters of coma is are unsettled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in a coma is disturbed by a design.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture or pattern made from small pieces of tile or glass.

clue.text: Rights reversed by servant maintaining a procedure

indicators.note: the whole assembled word is read backwards
the servant word holds the procedure word inside it

parts.note: a serf is a feudal servant
a mode is a way or procedure of doing something

explanation.surface: A servant overturns rights while keeping to protocol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' applies to the whole assembly after the servant holds the procedure, not to each piece separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: liberties or entitlements one is allowed to exercise.

clue.text: Gallic tower sounds like a pleasing sight!

indicators.note: the word is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: the Eiffel Tower is the famous tower in Paris

explanation.surface: Admiring the view of the famous Paris landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for something or someone very attractive to look at.

clue.text: One of crowd in old, upturned craft

parts.note: EX means former or old

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned up, so read backwards

parts.note: art is a craft or skill

explanation.surface: A crowd member in an old capsized boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat; it is skill, ART, which 'upturned' reverses to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is one of the crowd of background performers.

indicators.note: the word for stopped goes around the word for shower

parts.note: rested means paused or stopped
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: Someone halted outside a shower while being held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in check, kept under control: a past participle synonym.

parts.note: to win is to prevail

explanation.surface: Doubling up in time to come out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin or double is an exact counterpart of someone.

clue.text: Escapist looking for mixed choir round street

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the street abbreviation
the word choir is mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone avoiding reality hunting for a choir in a nearby street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' makes OCHRI from choir, and 'round' puts ST inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is said to bury its head in the sand, so the word describes someone avoiding unpleasant facts.

clue.text: Observe the bear, scrambling to exist

indicators.note: the letters of the bear are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching a bear clambering about trying to survive.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe is to live, to be alive: a verb synonym for existing.
